rockets.keyAdvance: The world's first gunpowder-propelled rocket and the earliest multi-stage rocket design.
rockets.triviaFact: True self-propelled rocket versions became widespread across China by the 12th-13th centuries.

rockets.keyAdvance: The world's first liquid-propellant rocket, launched by Robert Goddard on March 26, 1926.
rockets.triviaFact: Its historic first flight lasted only 2.5 seconds and the rocket landed in a nearby cabbage patch.

rockets.keyAdvance: The first long-range ballistic missile and the first rocket capable of reaching space.
rockets.triviaFact: The V-2 was the first man-made object to reach the edge of space.

rockets.keyAdvance: The first orbital launch vehicle in history, launched on October 4, 1957.
rockets.triviaFact: The R-7 is the only rocket family that has been continuously flying, in evolved form, since the dawn of the Space Age - the longest-serving rocket design in history.

rockets.keyAdvance: The most powerful rocket ever flown successfully, with the capability to send astronauts to the Moon.
rockets.triviaFact: At 363 feet tall, Saturn V was taller than the Statue of Liberty and generated the thrust of 85 Hoover Dams.

rockets.keyAdvance: The first reusable orbital spacecraft, first launched on April 12, 1981.
rockets.triviaFact: Its Solid Rocket Boosters were recovered from the ocean after launch and flown again on later missions.

rockets.keyAdvance: The first orbital-class rocket booster to land and be reused.
rockets.triviaFact: Falcon 9 achieved the first successful vertical landing of an orbital booster in December 2015, and the first re-flight of a used booster in March 2017.

rockets.keyAdvance: A fully reusable super-heavy lift vehicle designed for Moon and Mars missions.
rockets.triviaFact: Starship is the largest rocket ever built, and its April 2023 flight was the first integrated test of the full vehicle.
